key_idea: Shrink edges of two different length classes in a hypothetical periodic hat tiling to zero, which gives coupled periodic chevron and comet polyiamond tilings. The period lattices must then be related by an affine map that scales area by 2/3. A number-theoretic norm argument (m^2+mn+n^2) rules out that map being a similarity, while strip and orientation-balance counting forces it to be one.
reason: Coupling three tilings through the Tile(a,b) continuum is surprising, and the contradiction pits arithmetic against geometry, which is striking and explains how the shape family enforces aperiodicity. The execution still leans on worm/strip bookkeeping, per-case vector tables read off figures, and orientation-frequency balancing, so the argument is clever but not inevitable or easy to hold in one's head.
recognized: Smith, Myers, Kaplan, Goodman-Strauss, 'An aperiodic monotile' (the hat), Section 3 coupling proof
